subject: Urgent: Seneca tranche contention — request for allocation decision
messages:
From: Liam Foster <liam.foster@seneca.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@seneca.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Concern: Dedicated tranche being reallocated

Olga / Rishi,

Thanks for the quick answers on the contract redlines — one last item has cropped up on our side that we need to resolve before signature. Our infra team reported that a portion of the 120 GPU tranche we committed to (Q4 reserved lane) shows as "available for reassign" in your internal allocation snapshot. That would materially affect our launch runway.

We need confirmation that our reserved tranche will be held (no preemption) through the committed period, or a proposed mitigation (partial hold + guaranteed burst) we can accept in writing. Can you please escalate to capacity ops and provide a decision by EOD next Tuesday (2028-07-25)? This is the gating item for our procurement.

Attached: high-level launch schedule and expected peak tokens per minute.

Appreciate quick help here — Liam
Senior Procurement, Seneca AI

Attachments: seneca-tranche-request-attachments.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Liam Foster <liam.foster@seneca.ai>, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concern: Dedicated tranche being reallocated

Liam — thanks for the note and flag. Olga / team: looping in Ben and Laura from Sales ops so we can triage.

Preliminary context: the allocation you saw aligns with a rolling "soft reclaim" policy we run when demand spikes across multi-deal commitments. For SEN-4712 specifically, there is an active short-term overlap with a large burst request from a different customer (internal id: NEX-209) that consumes spare headroom in the same GPU pool for the next 72 hours. That said, the contract we drafted for Seneca includes language for a reserved tranche; I want to avoid any contract/regret mismatch.

Options I see:
- Option A: Hold the full 120 GPUs as a hard reservation and kick the burden to the preemption buffer — requires approval from capacity committee and will impact other customers' short-term burst windows.
- Option B: Commit to a 90 GPU hard reservation + guaranteed 30 GPU burst at a capped price and latency SLO; preserves some headroom for bursts.
- Option C: Offer a stepped reservation (60 / 90 / 120) linked to milestones (go-live, week 1, week 4) and a rollback plan if upstream concurrency persists.

I'm putting a request into CAP-8921 for an expedited allocation review. Ben / Laura: can Capacity Ops accelerate the decision matrix and provide the operational impact (cost delta + affected deals) by 7/25 EOD?

—Rishi
Head of Dedicated Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 11:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concern: Dedicated tranche being reallocated

Team — quick operational update from Capacity Ops (I pulled the heatmap and included a sanitized export). Two fast facts: 1) NEX-209 has a confirmed one-week burst window starting 7/22 for a paid performance trial; 2) there is ~18% spare headroom in the pool today but that will drop to ~2% during the trial peak.

Recommended path for the commercial team to avoid a procurement stall:
- Approve Option B (90 hard reserved / 30 burst) with a 10% premium on the burst tokens for the trial week, and a one-time goodwill credit for Seneca equal to 5% of the monthly committed spend if the trial causes any SLA blips.
- Ask NEX-209 to shift non-critical burst jobs outside the 18:00-23:00 UTC window where Seneca forecasts peak usage. We can route some of their low-priority jobs to a cross-region pool if they accept slightly higher latency.

Operational impacts and links: CAP-8921 (decision record), capacity-heatmap-2028-07.csv (attached).

Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Operations (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity-heatmap-2028-07.csv
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Liam Foster <liam.foster@seneca.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Decision and short-term plan: SEN-4712 tranche allocation

Liam / Elena — thanks again for flagging and for patience while we ran the allocation review. Below is the decision and the operational commitments Redwood will make to remove this as a gating item for your procurement: 

Decision (effective immediately):
- Redwood will convert the Seneca Q4 commitment to a 90 GPU hard reservation + 30 GPU guaranteed burst (Option B). That burst is contractually capped at the agreed burst premium and backed by an operational escalation path.

Compensating commitments:
- For the one-week Nex-209 trial (7/22–7/29) we will apply a 5% goodwill credit to the Seneca monthly invoice if any latency or capacity degradation is traced to that trial.
- We will run priority routing for Seneca traffic during your declared peak window (18:00–23:00 UTC) and re-route non-critical NEX-209 jobs to a cross-region pool where feasible.
- Redwood Capacity Ops will provide a nightly short report for the first two weeks after go-live (metrics: reserved utilization, burst activations, average token latency).

Next steps / timeline:
- Legal will insert the burst language and the 5% credit clause into exhibit B; Rishi / Laura to share final redline by EOD 7/26.
- Ben / Capacity Ops will confirm the pool mappings and hand-off runbook by 7/27.
- Liam to confirm acceptance and sign-off so procurement can finalize the PO.

Please reply to this thread to confirm acceptance or call me directly if you'd like to discuss a different mix. We want to keep Seneca's launch on schedule while being transparent about the operational tradeoffs.

Best,
Olga Petrov
VP, Sales Operations (Acting)
Redwood Inference
